earlier_scan.source_named: Only survey/comparative refs on Glottolog page (Barreteau & Dieu 2000 inventory; Gravina 2014 comparative Central Chadic); no descriptive grammar or phonology of Ngwaba located.

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalog, 'OLAC resources in and about the Ngwaba language' (Internet Archive copy, up-to-date as of 15 Aug 2024).
sources.note: Only two records: the Glottolog languoid page and the Ethnologue entry. No archived wordlist, recordings, grammar or phonology for ngw in any OLAC archive.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019 [file dated Sept 2020]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, Edition IV. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry '343. Ngwaba', printed p. 75 (PDF p. 103).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The entry gives only: alternate names Gombi, Goba; Adamawa State, Gombi LGA at Fachi and Gudumiya; 'less than 1000' speakers; 'Chadic: Biu-Mandara sub-branch A: Bata group'; 'Source(s) Blench (1987)' (the Atlas defines Source(s) as the author's own field visit or personal communication). No Refs line at all: no wordlist, phonology, grammar or dictionary is listed, whereas neighbouring entries carry 'Wordlist: Kraft (1981)' etc. The Atlas's classification index (p. ~ 'Biu-Mandara / Tera group') lists Ngwaba under Tera, not Bata.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: the reconstruction of the phonology and lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the linguistic history of the Central Chadic languages. Utrecht: LOT (LOT 375).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about Ngwaba stress. Table 3 'Lexical data sources' (p. 16) reads 'Ngwaba [ngw] Bata none', i.e. Gravina had no Ngwaba data; the reconstruction explicitly excludes 'tone or stress'. Ngwaba is only named as one of the twelve Bata-group languages (pp. 27, 47-48, 3.3.1).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. [2006, circulation draft]. Classification of Afroasiatic (AALIST). 15 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; Ngwaba appears only as a name in the Central Chadic, Tera group list (p. 6).

sources.citation: Ethnologue, 14th (2000), 15th (2005) and 16th (2009) edition entries for Ngwaba [ngw], read through the the Internet Archive.
sources.note: Nothing linguistic beyond classification 'Afro-Asiatic, Chadic, Biu-Mandara, A, A.8'; population 10,000 (1993 CAPRO); Gombi LGA at Fachi and Guduniya, and Hong LGA, 2 villages; 14th ed.: 'Investigation needed: intelligibility with Nzanyi'.

sources.citation: Endangered Languages Project, page for Ngwaba [ngw] (Internet Archive copy).
sources.note: Nothing; its four sources are Ethnologue 16 (2009), UNESCO Atlas (Moseley 2010), the World Oral Literature Project, and Fakuade, Gambo & Bashir 2003 (a language-shift questionnaire survey: 33% of Ngwaba respondents use Ngwaba with parents/children).

No descriptive reference at all: only Gravina 2014 pp. 47-48 and Barreteau & Dieu 2000 pp. 65-66 (classification comments), Campbell et al. 2022 and Lewis 2009 (endangerment). Alternate names Goba, Gombi, Enguaba.
Nothing; stubs citing only Ethnologue and Blench 2006. The Biu-Mandara page notes Ngwaba is placed in Bata (A.8) by some and in Tera (A.1) by Blench.

sources.citation: Fakuade, Gbenga, Matudi Gambo & Abdullahi Bashir. 2003. Language shift from mother tongues towards Fulfulde in Adamawa State, Nigeria: causes and consequences. Anthropological Linguistics 45(3): 296-315.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey including Ngwaba respondents; the only refereed article that treats Ngwaba at all. Would not give a stress statement but would confirm current location, vitality and the Ngwaba/Nzanyi relationship.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 1987. Unpublished field notes / wordlist from a 1987 visit to the Ngwaba (the only source given in the Atlas of Nigerian Languages entry 343, 'Source(s) Blench (1987)').
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only primary data on Ngwaba that is known to exist at all; a Blench survey wordlist would show tone marking and could carry a note on prosody, though a stress statement is unlikely. Ask Blench directly whether the 1987 Ngwaba list survives.

sources.note: Only to verify coverage: Blench's Atlas and Gravina 2014 indicate Kraft has no Ngwaba/Gombi list, so this is a low-priority check; even if present, Kraft lists mark tone, not stress.
